transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I can’t stop checking my work. I do bookkeeping, and I keep going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again, even when I know I already checked them. Sometimes I stay for hours after everyone else has left because I feel like if I don’t check just one more time, something bad will happen and it’ll be my fault.
Do you ever have thoughts or images pop into your mind that you find upsetting or that don’t feel like they belong to you?

Yes. It’s usually about work. Even after I know the numbers match, I’ll suddenly think, “What if I missed some hidden mistake?” Like in payroll or taxes, and then someone’s check won’t go through or the firm will get in trouble.

I try to push it out of my head because I know I already looked, but it comes right back. It makes me feel like I can’t trust what I just saw with my own eyes.
When you go back to check your work, does it help calm the worry or stop the bad thoughts from coming back, at least for a little while?

Yes, it does for a little bit. When I check the spreadsheet again, I feel calmer for a moment, like maybe I caught it or proved it’s okay. But then the doubt comes back, and I feel like I need to go over the calculations one more time. That’s how I end up staying hours after everyone else leaves, because it feels like if I stop, something bad could happen and it would be my fault.
Do these worries about making a mistake ever feel irrational or excessive to you, even while you’re experiencing them?

Yes. I mean, part of me knows it’s too much. I can see the numbers match, and I’ll still get this thought that maybe there’s one hidden mistake in payroll or taxes and someone’s check won’t go through, or the firm will get in trouble. I try to push it away, but it just comes back, and then it feels like I can’t even trust what I just saw.
